_about: PRO batch 47: era 4, The Veteran (34-37), set 3.

scenarios.title: The Family Retreat
scenarios.text: The whole family takes a week off together, the first in years: a rented house on a lake, no phones, a canoe nobody knows how to steer.

choices.label: Be completely there
choices.result: Phone in a drawer, all week. You learn to steer the canoe, badly, and everyone remembers the day you fell in.

choices.label: Plan something special each day
choices.result: A plan for every day: fishing, a hike, a night of board games. It's a lot, and the kids love the board games most.

choices.label: Invite {parent} along
choices.result: {parent}, invited for the second half of the week. Three generations around one table, and he tells stories you've never heard.

scenarios.title: The Coaching Clinic Offer
scenarios.text: A college wants you to run its kicking clinic every summer: two weeks, two hundred kids, and the promise of a full-time job when you're ready.

choices.label: Run it this summer
choices.result: This summer, and every summer after. You're exhausted and happy by August, and the college coach asks if you're ready yet.

choices.label: Agree for after you retire
choices.result: After you retire, you tell them, and they put it in writing. It's a door, and it's comforting to know it's there.

choices.label: Send a younger kicker instead
choices.result: A younger retired kicker, recommended by you, runs it instead. He's great at it, the kids love him, and he thanks you every single summer.

scenarios.title: The Broadcasting Tryout
scenarios.text: A network asks you to call one game during your off week, in the booth, beside a play-by-play announcer who's been doing it for thirty years.

choices.label: Do it and love it
choices.result: You do it, and you love it: the rhythm, the replays, the jokes. The network calls on Monday with an offer for after football.

choices.label: Prepare obsessively
choices.result: Seven days of preparation: every roster, every kicker's history, every stadium's wind. You're stiff for the first quarter and excellent after it.

choices.label: Rest on the off week
choices.result: Your off week stays completely off. The network books someone else, and the producer says to call whenever you're ready, any year.

scenarios.title: The Old Rival's Comeback
scenarios.text: {tyler} is attempting a comeback after two years out, and he calls to ask your advice. He sounds hopeful in a way that worries you.

choices.label: Help him train
choices.result: A month of training together in the offseason, on the old high school field. He's better than you expected, and he gets a tryout.

choices.label: Tell him the truth
choices.result: The truth, as kindly as you can: the league is younger now, and so is the leg he needs. He thanks you, and tries anyway.

choices.label: Make him a call
choices.result: A call to a special teams coach you trust, with {tyler}'s name. He gets a workout, and whatever happens, he got his chance.

scenarios.title: Signed for Your Experience
scenarios.text: A new club signs you for your experience after a spring of silence, and the locker room is skeptical. Someone has written 'how old?' on the tape above your locker.

choices.label: Leave the tape up
choices.result: The tape stays up, and you sign it with a flourish. By October the room has stopped wondering and started asking you questions instead.

choices.label: Earn it in a week
choices.result: Your best practices in years, every day, until the young players talk about them at dinner. Nobody writes on your locker again all season.

choices.label: Find the young specialists
choices.result: The young specialists, found and taken to lunch on the first day. They become your biggest defenders before the first game even arrives.

scenarios.title: The Locker Room Story Time
scenarios.text: Young players have started gathering around your locker after practice for stories: the old coaches, the bad flights, the season the stadium flooded and the team practiced in a hangar.

choices.label: Tell the stories
choices.result: The stories, every day for twenty minutes, until it becomes a ritual. One of the rookies starts writing them down.

choices.label: Hide a lesson in every story
choices.result: Every story, with a small lesson tucked inside it somewhere. The young players don't notice, and they learn every one of them anyway.

choices.label: Keep it to Fridays
choices.result: Fridays only, you announce, so you can get home for dinner. Fridays quickly become the best day of the week in the locker room.

scenarios.title: The Last Charity Game
scenarios.text: You play in the charity game you've hosted for years, maybe for the last time: same field, same kids, a sold-out crowd that knows the anniversary.

choices.label: Kick with every kid
choices.result: Every kid in the clinic gets one kick with you, all hundred and twenty of them. It takes three hours, and nobody leaves early.

choices.label: Hand it to someone else
choices.result: The event, handed to a younger player at halftime, with a speech and a handshake. It will outlast you now, which is what you wanted for it.

choices.label: Enjoy it like a fan
choices.result: For once, enjoyed from the sideline like a fan. You watch your kids run the concession stand and laugh all afternoon.

scenarios.title: The Final Season Tour Idea
scenarios.text: Your agent pitches a farewell season tour you haven't agreed to: gifts in every stadium, a documentary crew, a jersey patch. You haven't even decided to retire.

choices.label: Say no to the tour
choices.result: No tour, you tell your agent. You'll decide when you decide, and nobody can sell a goodbye you haven't said yet.

choices.label: Agree, if you retire
choices.result: If, and only if, you retire. Your agent agrees and keeps the whole plan in a drawer, ready to go, with your name on the folder.

choices.label: Ask your family
choices.result: Your family, asked what they'd want. The kids want the tour; {love_interest} wants a quiet goodbye. You keep both in mind.

scenarios.title: The Rookie Who Calls You 'Sir'
scenarios.text: A rookie calls you 'sir' in the hallway, and he means it completely. The specialists who heard it will never, ever let you forget it.

choices.label: Insist on your first name
choices.result: Your first name, insisted on, kindly but firmly. He tries for a week and keeps slipping, and the specialists keep a running score.

choices.label: Earn the respect
choices.result: The respect, earned every day: you show up first and help him with his plant foot. He keeps calling you 'sir', and now you understand why.

choices.label: Call him 'sir' back
choices.result: 'Sir', said right back to him, every day in the hallway. It becomes a running joke, and then, slowly, a real friendship.

scenarios.title: The Lost Step
scenarios.text: Your range is shrinking, and the coaches have adjusted the kicking chart without telling you. You find out when the long attempts go to the other kicker in practice.

choices.label: Ask to see the chart
choices.result: The chart, asked for directly. {coach} shows you, apologizes for not telling you first, and you start working on the numbers together.

choices.label: Win the long ones back
choices.result: The long kicks, won back in practice: extra work, every evening, until the chart changes again. It takes a month.

choices.label: Own the short ones
choices.result: The short and medium kicks, owned completely in every practice. You become the most accurate kicker in the league inside forty-five yards.

scenarios.title: The Family Business Offer
scenarios.text: {sibling} wants you to join their business when you retire: a landscaping company with twelve trucks, a good name in town, and a sign they've already designed with both your names.

choices.label: Say yes, for after
choices.result: Yes, for after. {sibling} sends you a photo of the sign the same night, and you start learning the business on Mondays.

choices.label: Invest instead of joining
choices.result: Money for two more trucks, but your own path after football. {sibling} understands, and the trucks have your name on the door anyway.

choices.label: Tell them you need time
choices.result: Time, you tell {sibling} honestly over the phone. They say the sign isn't going anywhere, and neither are they, whatever you decide.

scenarios.title: The Fan Who Has Seen Every Game
scenarios.text: A fan has been to every one of your home games since you arrived, always in the same seat, and asks through the team for a photo at what might be the last one.

choices.label: Meet her on the field
choices.result: On the field, before warmups, with a photographer and a signed ball. She brings a scrapbook of every ticket stub.

choices.label: Invite her to practice
choices.result: A practice pass, a lunch with the specialists, a tour of the locker room. She cries at the locker, and so does {holder}.

choices.label: Send a letter and a jersey
choices.result: A long letter and a signed jersey, delivered to her seat before kickoff. She frames both, and she writes back on lined paper.

scenarios.title: The Body Scan
scenarios.text: A full-body scan shows every injury you've ever had, in color, on a big screen: the hip, the ankle, the hamstring, three things you didn't know about.

choices.label: Go through it with the doctor
choices.result: Every spot, explained by the doctor, slowly. It's sobering and useful, and you leave with a plan for each one.

choices.label: Show it to {love_interest}
choices.result: The scan, shown at home on a laptop. {love_interest} looks for a long time and says, 'You've been busy,' and you both laugh.

choices.label: Keep kicking
choices.result: Kicking, the very next morning, as usual. The scan is a map of the past, and your leg still works perfectly well today.
